    RCT/ARCT No. 60/2018 & 14/2019                                     Page 2 of 16 pages
    Mukesh Kumar (since deceased) through LRs vs M/s Gargson           GIRISH KATHPALIA Digitally signed by GIRISH KATHPALIA
                                                                                        Date: 2022.02.17 15:25:36 +05'30'
     COMMON JUDGMENT
1. These two appeals under cite8†Section 38 of the Delhi Rent Control Act filed by the unsuccessful landlords to assail order and judgment dated 05.05.2018 (whereby the eviction petition on the ground stipulated under cite9†Section 14(1)(b) Delhi Rent Control Act was dismissed) and order dated 11.01.2019 (whereby in the same petition, benefit under cite9†Section 14(2) of the Act was granted) are taken up together for disposal on account of same factual matrix.
On service of notice, the respondent tenant entered appearance through counsel to oppose the appeal. I heard learned counsel for both sides and perused the trial court record.
2. Briefly stated, circumstances leading to the present appeals are as follows.
2.1 Shri Mukesh Kumar, the now deceased predecessor of the appellants filed an eviction petition against the respondent M/s Gargson, a sole proprietorship concern of Shri Om Prakash Gupta under cite9†Section 14(1)(a) &(b) of the cite10†Delhi Rent Control Act , pleading that being owner and landlord of shop No.
3649, Gali Rura Achar Wali, Chawri Bazar, Delhi (hereinafter referred to as "the tenanted shop") he inducted the respondent as a tenant with effect from 01.01.1979 by way of rent receipt and the respondent started carrying on business of plastic goods from there; that subsequently, the respondent unauthorizedly sublet the tenanted shop to M/s Gargson Autoplast, who is carrying on similar business from the tenanted RCT/ARCT No.
60/2018 & 14/2019 Page 3 of 16 pages Mukesh Kumar (since deceased) through LRs vs M/s Gargson GIRISH KATHPALIA Digitally signed by GIRISH KATHPALIA Date: 2022.02.17 15:25:17 +05'30' shop; that initial rent of the tenanted shop was Rs. 120/- per month, which was enhanced time to time and lastly to Rs.
1200/- per month with effect from 01.02.2002 by way of notice dated 05.06.2002 in consonance with law laid down by the Hon'ble Delhi High Court in the case of cite11†Raghunandan Saran Ashok Saran (HUF) vs Union of India , 95 (2002) DLT 508 DB ; that despite service of notice dated 05.06.2002, the respondent did not pay rent arrears, so was liable to be evicted on the grounds stipulated under cite9†Sections 14(1)(a) &(b) of the cite10†Delhi Rent Control Act .
2.2 Written statement on behalf of respondent was filed by Shri Arun Kumar Garg before the trial court, pleading that the tenanted shop had been let out to him as proprietor of M/s Gargson in 1979 and he continues to be in possession as proprietor of M/s Gargson; that rent of the tenanted shop was always paid by him, being proprietor of M/s Gargson, in cash and at times through cheques but the landlord did not issue rent receipts; that there was and is no proprietor of M/s Gargson by the name Shri Om Prakash Gupta; that rent of the tenanted shop was revised time to time from 140/- per month to Rs.
170/- per month, which was paid; that for the period from 01.04.2001 to 31.10.2002, the respondent sent the rent by money order but the landlord refused to accept the same, so the respondent deposited the rent under cite12†Section 27 of the Delhi Rent Control Act in the court of Rent Controller; that legal notice dated 05.06.2002 was never served upon the respondent; that M/s Gargson Autoplast is another proprietorship concern of Shri Arun Kumar Garg, which is a manufacturing unit operating exclusively from 69, RCT/ARCT No.

> 2.3 After his death, the eviction petitioner Shri Mukesh Kumar was substituted with his legal representatives (the appellants herein), who filed a replication denying the contents of the written statement and reaffirmed the petition contents. In their replication, the appellants further pleaded that subsequent to death of Shri Mukesh Kumar on 25.12.2011, the appellants issued another legal notice dated 03.09.2012, calling upon the respondent to pay rent of the tenanted shop at a rate of Rs.
206/- per month with effect from 01.11.2012 but despite service of the said notice on 11.09.2012, the respondent did not pay arrears of rent and thereby committed second default, so the respondent is liable to be evicted.
> 2.4 On the basis of above rival pleadings, trial was carried out before the learned Additional Rent Controller in which both sides examined one witness each.
> 2.5 After hearing both sides, the learned Additional Rent Controller by way of the impugned order and judgment dated 05.05.2018 dismissed the eviction petition so far as ground under cite9†Section 14(1)(b) of the Delhi Rent Control Act is concerned, but allowed the petition on the ground stipulated under cite9†Section 14(1)(a) of the Act, posting the matter for inquiry under cite9†Section 14(2) of the Act.
Thereafter, vide the impugned order dated 11.01.2019, the learned Additional Rent Controller extended benefit under cite9†Section 14(2) of the Act to the respondent. Hence, the present appeals of the RCT/ARCT No.

60/2018 & 14/2019 Page 6 of 16 pages Mukesh Kumar (since deceased) through LRs vs M/s Gargson GIRISH KATHPALIA Digitally signed by GIRISH KATHPALIA Date: 2022.02.17 15:24:19 +05'30' 3.2 As regards the ground under cite9†Section 14(1)(b) of the Act, the learned Additional Rent Controller arrived at the findings that the petition as well as the evidence lacked material particulars with respect to the alleged subtenancy; that the eviction petitioner had not conclusively established that the respondent had sublet or parted with possession with the tenanted shop without consent of the landlord;
and that the photographs filed by the eviction petitioner himself show that the tenanted shop is in possession of M/s Gargson, who was inducted as a tenant and there is no evidence to show that M/s Gargson, inducted as a tenant was a different entity, so ground under cite9†Section 14(1)(b) of the Act failed.
4. During final arguments, both learned counsel took me through trial court records in support of their respective contentions.
4.1 Learned counsel for appellants contended that neither of the orders impugned in these appeals is sustainable in the eyes of law.
It was argued that the respondent failed to adduce any documentary evidence to show that proprietor of M/s Gargson was not Shri Om Prakash but Shri Arun Kumar Garg; and that Shri Arun Kumar Garg did not personally step into the witness box and the solitary witness examined on behalf of respondent was wife of Shri Arun Kumar, so it calls for adverse inference against the respondent.
4.2 On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent contended that there is no infirmity in the impugned orders and judgment. It was argued that despite the respondent having denied service of notices dated 05.06.2002 and 03.09.2012, neither of those notices was put to the respondent in cross examination. It was further argued that the appellants never sought modification of order under cite13†Section 15(1) of the Act and compliance with the order was duly carried out.
4.3 In rebuttal, counsel for appellants argued that both notices were duly proved with the help of postal record, but the learned Additional Rent Controller did not even discuss the second notice which was dated 03.09.2012.
